newsitem.title: USA: Stocks, bonds fall on rate fears, dollar rise.
newsitem.headline: Stocks, bonds fall on rate fears, dollar rise.

text.p: Stocks and bonds fell on Friday as Wall Street worried about interest rates ahead of a slew of economic reports next week.
The dollar rose against the German mark and recouped losses vs. the Japanese yen as Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reaffirmed support for a strong dollar.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 53.38 points, or 0.8 percent, to 6,738.87, after sliding more than 60 points earlier in light trading.

The Dow's drop trimmed its gain to 35.32 points for the week, as blue chips dipped in each of the three sessions after jumping 173 points on Tuesday in the 30-stock index's second-largest point gain ever.
In the broader market, declining issues outnumbered gainers by 1,658 to 795 on volume of 414 million the New York Stock Exchange.
"Basically, attention is focused on next week," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest, "and next week is truly going to be hell week."

Investors appeared increasingly reluctant to bid up stocks just ahead of reports on employment and wages, gross domestic product, the National Association of Purchasing Management index and the Employment Cost Index, a key wage inflation gauge.

"We've got a bushel basket of important economic data next week that will largely confirm whether or not (Fed) Chairman Greenspan will follow through with a second monetary tightening," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management.
The Nasdaq Composite index fell 18.81 points to 1,209.29, down 13.28 on the week.

Bonds edged lower, with the 30-year Treasury down 4/32, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 7.14 percent from Thursday's close of 7.13 percent. The price and yield move in opposite directions.
The dollar rose to 1.7275 marks by the U.S. close from 1.7150 at Thursday's close and 126.30 yen from 126.08.
Soybean futures soared on rumours that China was buying from the United States and further drawing down already low stockpiles.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, soybeans for May delivery closed 20-3/4 cents a bushel higher at $8.67-3/4.

Corn prices benefited from the gains in soybeans and from fresh export demand. But cool, clear planting weather in the Midwest lent optimism about coming supplies. May corn closed up 1-1/2 cents a bushel at $2.94-1/2.

Wheat prices also closed higher on renewed concerns about harsh weather in Texas and Oklahoma hurting winter wheat already damged by last week's hard freeze. Wheat for May delivery traded in Chicago closed up 2 cents a bushel at $4.23-1/2.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index of leading stocks finished 18.8 points lower at 4,369.7 for a net gain of 59.2 points on the week. In Tokyo, the Nikkei average closed 85.21 points, or 0.46 percent, lower at 18,612.86, a rise of 260.72 points from seven days ago.
